task: predict Big Five personality traits of Twitter users
note: MLSMOTE (multilabel SMOTE) on BERT embeddings; XGBoost per trait; stratified 10-fold CV. Order of oversampling and CV not stated explicitly; before-split inferred from III.D wording and Table VI counts. Stakes: personality for hiring/career decisions.

task: flag fraudulent motor insurance claims
note: ADASYN and SMOTE balanced to 1:1 on Kaggle auto-insurance claims (fraud <25%); SVM, compared with SMOTE+RF from [3]. Split and resampling order never described; figure values only approximate in text. Stakes: customer's claim investigated/paid.

task: diagnose aero-engine wear faults from spectral oil data via extracted rules
note: New rule-extraction method (GA feature selection + support vector clustering rules); SMOTE only for aero-engine oil data (230/5/2). UCI comparisons with C4.5/BayesNet lack resampling. Measures 'other' = rule support/confidence. Domain could be transport.

task: na
note: Own method under rule B: Sec. 2.2, 3.2 and 5 present CBS (k-means, mini-cluster filtering, SMOTE) as a new strategy, compared with SMOTE, COS, CUS and Raw. Resampling inside training split (Sec. 3.4).

task: predict DNA-binding residues in protein sequences
note: ADASYN on positives + bootstrap undersampling into balanced subsets, CNN ensemble; no other resampling compared, so application under rule B. Sec. 2 puts ADASYN in training phase, but metric arithmetic shows non-natural test folds.

task: extract relations between entity pairs from news and Wikipedia text
note: New model (two aggregated PCNNs, OWA loss) plus partial random oversampling (copies until least/most class ratio >1/5) and class-weighted loss. Ablation without resampling reported only qualitatively. 'Weighted accuracy' = balanced accuracy.

task: screen urine GC-MS profiles for inborn errors of metabolism and classify 11 IEMs
note: Oversampler not named (imblearn; per-class rates by incidence, Suppl. Table S2), coded 'other'. Two-stage random forest; sampling scheme not compared with alternatives, so application under rule B. External test: 38 MMA cases from another lab.

task: classify toddlers' nutritional status into five categories
note: Single split at four ratios (60:40 to 90:10); best scheme chosen on test results. No model without SMOTE reported despite abstract's claim that SMOTE improved reliability. Stakes: each child's nutritional status.

task: flag fraudulent credit card transactions
note: Conditional GAN (CTGAN-inspired) used as is (B2): application. Baseline is unweighted; cost-weighted loss is part of the framework, no cost-only arm; cost curve sweeps thresholds for both. Results mostly trends; 5-fold CV mentioned without detail.

task: predict district heating pipe failures
note: Existing ROS, SMOTE, EVSG [9] plus K-means undersampling compared, OS/DS levels grid-tuned: application. Final RF with ROS+DS. Failures split temporally, non-failures randomly. Measures: FCLC AUC, AUC10, confusion matrix. Domain energy (district heating); industry plausible.

task: detect truck air pressure system failures
note: Conclusion claims before/after SMOTE analysis but no unresampled results shown. Only measure is IDA 2016 cost (10*FP+500*FN). MICE, PCA, SMOTE described on the 60,000 set. Domain industry (predictive maintenance); transport plausible.

task: na
note: No domain application: compares existing Random-SMOTE (Dong 2009) with no resampling, logit, on five generic UCI benchmarks (Glass, Haberman, Pima, Vowel, Wine). Resampling evaluation without application. Also resampled before the 2/3 split (Sec V-C).

task: diagnose coronary artery disease from clinical data
note: Pipeline: scaling, SMOTE to parity on whole data, extra-trees feature selection (36 features), SVM-RBF best. Sec IV says SMOTE made 'training data' representative, so before-split rests on pipeline order. Accuracy 95.16% (abstract) vs 95.79% (conclusion).

task: classify cancer type (33 tumor types) from mRNA and miRNA expression
note: Existing Borderline-SMOTE + Tomek links (Tomek coded undersampling) inside a GAT+DNN pipeline; contribution is the classifier: application. Compared models (XGBoost-AD, RF, KNN, etc.) are baselines. Domain medicine (framed as patient cancer diagnosis); bio plausible.

task: cluster park electricity users and rank energy storage potential
note: Unsupervised case study: K-means (K by SSE, silhouette, CH) on 50 users' daily loads, existing Borderline-SMOTE to balance clusters, Delphi-weighted TOPSIS ranking. Not compared with other resampling: application. No split, classifier or performance evaluation.

task: assess building fire risk level
note: Text file is the paper, font-shifted (+29 code points, digits lost); decoded to read. Existing SMOTE then expert-aided Bayesian network; no experiments, data or metrics shown (measures na) despite claimed validation. Domain: building fire hazard; other plausible.

task: detect maize lodging in field plots from UAV image features
note: SMOTE-ENN applied after the 70:30 split but to training and test sets separately (Table 5); tuning CV apparently on resampled training set. Before/after comparison uses different test sets. Tabular features extracted from UAV images.

task: detect DDoS attacks in IoT network traffic
note: Four boosting models x SMOTE/Borderline-SMOTE on CICDDoS2019 and KDDCUP99; no unresampled baseline. F1 named in abstract but absent from result tables; MAE, RMSE, training time coded other.

task: segment satellite images into village, mountain and river areas
note: Unsupervised FCM/possibilistic clustering on pixel intensities of two satellite images; resampling uses ground-truth labels; no split or CV, evaluated on the same images' original pixels. Compares ROS, RUS, SMOTE within the application.

task: detect noble-gas-instability fault precursors in vacuum ion pump pressure data
note: SMOTE (50% ratio) combined with cost-sensitive SVM vs cost-sensitive SVM alone; CNN cost-sensitive only. Four splits incl. cross-pump and temporal. 'Post-deployment' evaluation looks like retrospective run on 54 new pumps 2022-2025, so validation coded external.

task: distinguish treatment-induced effects from recurrent glioblastoma in MRI tissue-sample patches
note: Full text is the meeting abstract itself (Neuro-Oncology suppl. p. vii177), identical to record abstract. Oversampling method not named; read as plain oversampling of TxE samples. Test set is one third of patients withheld, same cohort.

task: classify low-grade glioma molecular subtypes (IDH, 1p/19q) from MRI radiomics
note: Radiomics features from MRI (tabular). Authors call the 42-patient test set external, but both parts are drawn from the same TCGA-LGG cohort (four sites), so validation coded internal. No unresampled baseline.

task: predict vector-borne diseases such as dengue and malaria from symptom records
note: Text inconsistent: abstract claims environmental/clinical data and precision/recall/F1, but data are a public 41-class symptom dataset and only accuracy is reported; K-Means used as classifier; mentions lung cancer. Abstract says 'oversampling'; text names SMOTE and undersampling.

task: classify stress level (low, moderate, high) from physiological and lifestyle data
note: Two datasets (hospital IT staff sensor data; UCI/Kaggle lifestyle survey), each split 80:20. Precision/recall/F1/AUC named but only accuracy reported. 'No sampling' baseline mentioned qualitatively only, confounded with PSS relabelling.

task: detect and classify vulnerability types in Solidity smart contract code
note: Code vulnerability detection: security/software borderline. vs_none from training accuracy/loss curves on imbalanced vs balanced data only; test metrics only for balanced data. Duplicated minority samples can fall in both train and test.

task: classify sentiment of Indonesian tweets about electric vehicles
note: Labels from TextBlob polarity after translation (not human labels). Conclusion says SMOTE balanced 'the training data', but test counts show the split was taken from the SMOTE-balanced set.

task: flag fraudulent credit card transactions in real time
note: Proposes CNN-LSTM classifier; SMOTE existing. Weighted loss also used, not compared. Table 1 metrics internally inconsistent (baseline F1 above P and R; implied test prevalence ~22%), so no rule-D basis. Stakes: transaction-level flag coded other.

task: recognize seven basic facial expressions from face images
note: SMOTE only on RAF-DB (one of three datasets); standard augmentation (x5) on CK+ for small size, not imbalance, so not listed. 'Entire dataset as input' may be a generic SMOTE description; coded nr.

task: classify water coverage ratio level (6 classes) in PEM fuel cell channel images
note: Oversampled copies are augmented (flip, random lighting). Text says balancing removes 'the imbalance of all data'; split described later; no explicit order statement. Boundary-near samples deleted from all data.

task: predict defect-prone software modules (NASA MDP datasets)
note: 'Pure' column lacks both SMOTE and feature selection (confounded). SMOTE test sizes do not equal exactly 20% of fully balanced counts; several SMOTE columns repeat across datasets (copy errors). Sec 3.1/5: balancing in preprocessing.

task: detect electricity theft (fraudulent consumers) from smart meter consumption data
note: Split/test protocol never described; GridSearchCV (cv=4) ran on the balanced data. Benchmarks SVM, LR, AdaBoost, DT, KNN, GB also with SMOTE-Tomek. Stakes: flags consumers for inspection.

task: detect coronary artery disease from clinical and work-related features
note: Contribution is 2HFS feature selection; SMOTE vs ADASYN compared but not presented as own method. 'Original data' rows lack both FS and balancing (confounded). Text and abstract disagree on which sampler gave 81.23%.

task: classify Alzheimer's disease stage from brain MRI
note: Kaggle 4-class MRI set with predefined train/test folders. Oversampling = rotated/flipped copies of minority images ('random oversampling augmentation'). Flowchart text says split after preprocessing, conflicting with Sec. II.B; coded stated. Training time also reported.

task: detect fraudulent bank account applications
note: Text says 80/20 split but counts fit a stratified 75/25 split (82,717+27,573; 8,272+2,757). Models trained on SMOTENC data; NearMiss set used for feature selection. vs_weights=yes: tuned vs default thresholds, both after SMOTENC. other=FPR.

task: screen patients for early type 2 diabetes onset
note: Datasets not named (UCI/Kaggle 'and population-specific'). 'Independent testing' not described as another source, coded internal. Before-split rests on the balanced test set only; a balanced test sample is the alternative. No no-resampling baseline.

task: segment aerial LiDAR point clouds into urban land-cover classes
note: PMNet fusion network is the contribution; Sec. 5.3 side experiment duplicates patches with >70% minor/medium-class points by flips (resampler other). Weighted cross-entropy in all runs, not compared. Avg.CA coded balanced-accuracy; other measure = MIoU.

task: predict software refactoring candidates
note: Five refactoring datasets x feature-selection variants = 30; nine classifiers reported (text says fifteen). Datasets and class ratios not described. Before-split from Sec. IV order plus metric arithmetic.

task: detect mental stress state (baseline, stress, amusement) from ECG and GSR
note: WESAD data. Train/test split method not described. Confusion-matrix orientation unclear; either reading gives an imbalanced test set. Number of features (70) chosen by accuracy on an unstated set.

task: detect fraudulent credit card transactions
note: European cardholder 2013 data (492/284,807). Reported metrics fit 3-7% test prevalence for baseline and SMOTE alike, inconsistent with the stated split; test_balanced nr. AUC about (recall+1)/2. class_weight=balanced in configs, not compared.

task: detect fraudulent credit card transactions
note: Kaggle European CCFD. Results inconsistent (text 97.58% accuracy vs Table II 93.8%; test size fits 30%, not stated 20%). Preprocessing names fields not in CCFD (attack_cat, is_ftp_login). KNN/CNN/NB figures cited from other papers.

task: classify dental disease (cavity, periodontitis, periapical infection) from panoramic X-rays
note: Contribution is the CNN IDD-Net; SMOTE-Tomek on 150x150 images of all 670 cases before the split, so test set holds synthetic images. Table 4 loss is categorical cross-entropy, coded log-loss.

task: identify patchouli variety from leaf images
note: Extreme learning machine on 14 handcrafted leaf features (morphology, wavelet, convex hull). Balanced-run accuracies are multiples of 1/70; imbalanced-run test had 28 items (30% of 91). Agriculture coded environment.

task: predict neonatal death from 2022 Kenya DHS survey records
note: Grid search used repeated 5-fold CV; SMOTE placement relative to those folds not described. Reported metrics come from the untouched 25% test set; accuracies sit near the 97.8% no-death base rate.

task: classify corn leaf images into three diseases or healthy
note: Arithmetic hints SMOTE spared the test set: SMOTE-arm test accuracies are multiples of 1/388, as in the original arm (10% of 4768 would be 477); Rule D covers only adverse codes, so nr kept.

task: classify retail customers into high-, medium- or low-value segments for precision marketing
note: Oversampling method never named (coded other). Three customer-value classes labelled from profit rate. Before-split read from step order; test balance follows from it. No no-resampling arm.

task: detect breast cancer from anthropometric and routine blood data (Coimbra)
note: Coimbra data: 64 patients, 52 controls. Test set had 11 items on original data, 12 after ADASYN. 36 learners incl. RUSBoosted Trees; precision/recall/F1 reported only for ADASYN arm.

task: classify a person's emotion from EEG signals
note: Layout hints SMOTE on all ~2100 records before the split (generic tutorial wording), not stated. Data source muddled (DEAP vs OpenNeuro). 'Oversampling and SMOTE' named; only SMOTE described. Medicine arguable for domain.

task: diagnose rolling-bearing fault condition from vibration signals
note: B2: standard DCGAN (4 conv layers, signals reshaped 70x70), no stated change, so application despite 'new DCGAN model' wording. Compared with ROS, RUS, SMOTE; SVM on 13 features. Test balanced by selection, not resampling.

task: predict defibrillation shock success (ROEA) from pre-shock VF ECG
note: Proposes 1D CNN on raw ECG. RF/kNN/SVM/AMSA comparison taken from authors' earlier paper with the same SMOTE preprocessing. Other = NPV. Acc 93.6 = mean of Sen and Spec, consistent with balanced folds.

task: predict type 2 diabetes from clinical attributes (PIDD)
note: Proposes CGLSTM; SVM/RF/KNN baselines. vs_none only via Table 5 ablation removing all preprocessing. Eq. 4 SMOTE description is nonstandard. Accuracy 97.84 exceeds sensitivity and specificity, so metrics are inconsistent; no arithmetic basis.

task: predict presence of heart disease from clinical variables
note: Transfer learning: pre-train on multi-hospital (Cleveland removed), fine-tune on Cleveland. External = zero-shot test on Cleveland site, same UCI family (authors' caveat). Mild imbalance (60/40). Table 14 ablation without SMOTE. DCA in Fig. 2.

task: predict fault-prone code elements in Java projects (BugHunter)
note: Sec II.6 states SMOTE applied solely to the training portion; Table V metrics nonetheless fit balanced test data (Rule D), so coded before-split. CV described inconsistently (10-fold vs eight segments). Seven learners compared.

task: classify upsilon states vs background in CMS dielectron events
note: Particle physics (CMS open data), multiclass, background over 90%. Compares seven SMOTE-family resamplers and weighted RF against plain RF; SMOTEN coded other-SMOTE-variant. Other = FPR, FNR, NPV. Single 80/20 split.

task: classify network traffic as normal or one of four attack types (NSL-KDD)
note: Text states SMOTE on whole data before split/CV, but reported test counts are natural and CV recall (90.15) is far below accuracy (99.79): coded nr. Smart-grid framing; NSL-KDD. No ET without SMOTE.

task: na
note: Own resampling method under Rule B: hybrid sampling (SMOTE then grouped NCL, Algorithm 1) presented as contribution and compared with SMOTE alone and no sampling (Table IV). NSL-KDD intrusion detection; resampling on training set only.

task: predict cell-penetrating peptides from aggregated physicochemical properties
note: Random oversampling with replacement to majority count (not SMOTE). Five learners compared; no run without oversampling. Reported RF metrics internally inconsistent (MCC .906 with accuracy .946), so no arithmetic basis. Student report.

task: classify OS family, vendor and device type of IP-connected devices from Nmap fingerprints
note: Comparative ML/DL study on Nmap DB; non-augmented vs SMOTE vs ADASYN for each of 11 models. 'other' measure = training/inference time; 'other' learner = QDA. Domain could arguably be IT operations (software).

task: na
note: Own resampling scheme under rule B: BBR-OFS searches the SMOTE balance ratio (rho to 1, step 0.1) by CV error, presented as core contribution, compared with weighted SVM. SRAM yield (industry) otherwise; SMOTE applied before 5-fold CV.

task: predict presence of heart disease from clinical features
note: Reported XGBoost metrics are internally inconsistent (accuracy exceeds both sensitivity and specificity) and match those the paper attributes to study [3]. Narrative order suggests SMOTE before the split but is not explicit.

task: predict whether a bank client subscribes to a term deposit after direct marketing
note: SMOTE in WEKA with VDM for nominal attributes; minority 5,289 oversampled 400% to 26,445 (text swaps class labels). Bank marketing coded business rather than finance. SMOTE lowered NB, KNN and SVM accuracy.

task: classify HRV before vs after smoking to find the most important HRV predictor
note: SMOTE (100%) doubled both balanced groups (20+20 to 40+40) to enlarge the sample, not to fix imbalance; t-tests also run on augmented data. Evaluation design unreported; metrics imply 16-18 test cases. HRV features coded tabular.

task: identify collapsed buildings from post-earthquake satellite imagery
note: Random over- and under-sampling compared with cost-sensitive class weights on SqueezeNet CNN; cost-sensitive best by Kappa. Spatially separate test regions of the same image coded internal. PA/UA mapped to recall/precision; non-collapsed PA/UA to specificity/other.

task: classify Android apps as benign or one of four malware categories for smart home controllers
note: Oversampling ratio tuned as an ordinary hyperparameter (best: minority at 90% of majority), not a new resampling procedure; coded application. Reported results inconsistent: all per-class SVM recalls below 0.66 yet accuracy 85.3%; one precision of 1.010.

task: classify corporations' social insurance debt default level (no, low, medium, high)
note: Compares eight existing resampling set-ups (ROS with OVO/OVA, RUS, iterative SMOTE, MDO, ADASYN, Global-CS, SOUP); Global-CS here is replication-based oversampling, not learner weights. Debtors are corporations. Micro precision differs from micro recall, inconsistent.

task: detect network intrusions (normal vs attack traffic)
note: Standard GAN and VAE-GAN (B2) generate samples for NSL-KDD; GNN-Transformer on KDD Cup 99 uses no resampling. No plain MLP baseline; comparison tables largely cite literature values. Split used for results not stated.

task: predict high-entropy alloy phase (BCC, FCC, BCC+FCC, HCP)
note: Each oversampler combined with cost-sensitive LightGBM; no cost-sensitive-only arm. Baseline LightGBM without resampling in Table 1. Materials science coded other. External check: 6 alloys from outside dataset, source unstated; main results 10-fold CV.

task: predict mortality of heart failure patients
note: Contribution is the IBS stacking classifier (DT, RF, GB, boosting; logistic meta-learner). SMOTE-ENN applied to the whole 299-record dataset, then feature selection, then 5-fold CV; text also states this order. No unresampled baseline.

task: na
note: No resampling at all: full text matches title and DOI (rGO buffer layer in perovskite solar cells). The record's abstract (credit-card fraud; over/undersampling, class weights; RF, XGBoost, DNN) belongs to a different paper; metadata mismatch.

task: predict defect-prone software modules
note: Pi sigma network, 70/30 split per NASA dataset; text never says whether SMOTE preceded the split, so codes rest on arithmetic. Unresampled PSNN reported only for CM1 (about 90% accuracy).

task: classify glioma grade (LGG vs HGG) from brain MRI
note: CV on SMOTE-augmented training set (synthetic cases in validation folds); main results on test sets. Filter hyperparameters tuned on test data. BRATS 2013 accuracy 97.6% unattainable on Table 2's 6-case test if cases are units.

task: detect fetal chromosomal aneuploidy from NIPT screening data
note: Contribution is cost-sensitive XGBoost (instance weights plus cost-based threshold); 'moderate oversampling' method unspecified (coded other); SMOTE-XGB baseline. Paper claims strict test separation but describes oversampling before the 60/20/20 split. Expected cost coded other.

task: predict 2-year MACE occurrence in acute coronary syndrome patients
note: Text: stratified 80/20 split, then sampling 'while training'; reported metrics nevertheless imply balanced test sets. Contribution is a stacking ensemble (seven base learners, RF meta-learner). Cluster Centroids coded undersampling.

task: na
note: Own method under rule B: OSS+SMOTE hybrid presented as contribution (with TWSVM) and compared with SVM+OSS and SVM+SMOTE; also no domain problem, only five generic UCI benchmark sets.

task: diagnose polycystic ovary syndrome from clinical screening features
note: Order stated explicitly: SMOTE and correlation feature selection on the full data before holdout/CV. Table 4 diagnostic metrics (Eq. 7-13, MedCalc, 95% CI) not legible in text; MSE/MAE/RMSE coded other; ROC scores read as ROC-AUC.

task: classify drinking water samples as fit or unfit for consumption
note: Not own method under B: plain SMOTE, contribution is bagged k-NN; comparisons only with no SMOTE. Sec. II order ambiguous, arithmetic decides. Extra Kaggle sets (water potability, Titanic, diabetes) are side experiments.

task: na
note: Own method under rule B: BDSK (k-means undersampling plus SMOTE on smaller 2-means minority cluster, target mean class size) presented as contribution and compared with RUS+SMOTE, k-means SMOTE, k-means undersampling; generic Tan corpus benchmark.

task: detect freeway traffic accidents in real time from loop-detector and weather data
note: Sec. 2.1 says the 32 accidents were raised to 85,182 (all non-accident cases), conflicting with training-only SMOTE; reported metrics fit a natural test. Engineered loop-detector/weather features coded tabular. FAR (FP/all cases) coded other.

task: classify sentiment of tweets about Islamophobia after the Christchurch attack
note: Order not described (Sec. 2.1.4: 10-fold CV on processed data, SMOTE added); arithmetic decides. Labels from VADER, not human. Text says 2936 tweets but metrics imply 2657. Web app built, no results from use.
